questions.stem: A patient with a new HIV diagnosis wants dolutegravir plus lamivudine starting today. Which test must come first?
questions.explanation: A is correct: test for hepatitis B first, because several backbone drugs also treat it and the two-drug pill is only for patients with hepatitis B ruled out. B, C, and D are not the key test taught.

questions.stem: What do most patients start for HIV?

options.text: An integrase inhibitor plus two backbone drugs

questions.explanation: C is correct: most patients start an integrase inhibitor, like bictegravir or dolutegravir, plus two backbone drugs, often in one pill. A, B, and D are not the usual starting regimen.

questions.stem: Match each drug class to the step it blocks. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Integrase inhibitors stop it getting in
Entry blockers stop the virus getting in
Backbone drugs stop it copying its genes
Integrase inhibitors stop it inserting genes into our cells
Protease inhibitors stop it building new virus

questions.explanation: B, C, D, and E are correct as taught. A is wrong because entry blockers stop the virus getting in.

questions.stem: Which are among the five rules before starting HIV treatment? Select all that apply.

options.text: Check the gene test before abacavir
Skip testing if the patient feels well
Send a resistance test at baseline

questions.explanation: A, B, D, and E are correct as taught; spacing from antacids, calcium, and iron is the fifth. C is wrong because testing comes first.

questions.stem: Which statement about prevention before exposure is correct?

options.text: It can start without an HIV test
Confirm a negative test first, and retest regularly
It must start within 72 hours of one exposure

questions.explanation: B is correct: confirm a negative test first and retest regularly; using prevention doses in someone already infected breeds resistance. A is unsafe. C and D describe prevention after exposure.

questions.stem: Which prevention-before-exposure options are taught? Select all that apply.

options.text: A cabotegravir shot every 2 months after starter doses
A lenacapavir shot every 6 months after starting

questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct as taught. D and E are not options described in the video.

questions.stem: When must prevention after exposure start, and for how long?
questions.explanation: C is correct: start as soon as possible, no later than 72 hours, then take it for 28 days. A starts too late and is too short. B describes ongoing treatment. D is too short.

questions.stem: An exposure happened 80 hours ago. Should prevention after exposure start now?

options.text: Generally no; test now, test later, and offer ongoing prevention

questions.explanation: C is correct: past 72 hours, starting is not expected to help, so test now, test again later, and offer ongoing prevention if risk continues. A, B, and D ignore the 72-hour limit.

questions.stem: A patient on the bictegravir combination pill starts a calcium supplement. What is the best advice?

options.text: Take them together on an empty stomach

questions.explanation: B is correct: calcium or iron can be taken together with bictegravir if food is on board. A lowers absorption. C is unnecessary. D is not the fix.

questions.stem: How should bictegravir be spaced from aluminum or magnesium antacids?

options.text: Take bictegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after

questions.explanation: B is correct: take bictegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum or magnesium antacids. A applies to calcium or iron, not these antacids. C ignores the interaction. D is not the taught spacing.
